title: M/S SWASTIK ENTERPRISES versus UTTARAKHAND POWER CORPORATION LIMITED
judges: ["Hon'ble Shri Justice Manoj Kumar Gupta,Hon'ble Mr. Justice Subhash Upadhyay"]

paras.text:
UKHC010166192026
2026:UHC:8559-DB
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
THE HON'BLE CHIEF JUSTICE MR. MANOJ KUMAR GUPTA
AND
THE HON'BLE JUSTICE MR. SUBHASH UPADHYAY
Writ Petition (M/B) No.788 of 2026
23rd September, 2026
M/s Swastik Enterprises -----Petitioner
Versus
Uttarakhand Power Corporation Limited and Others
----Respondents
----------------------------------------------------------------------
Presence:-
Mr. Bhuwan Bhatt and Mr. Prince Chauhan, learned counsel for
the petitioner.
Mr. Dharmendra Barthwal, learned counsel for the respondents.
----------------------------------------------------------------------
JUDGMENT : (per Mr. Manoj Kumar Gupta C. J.)
1. Heard learned counsel for the parties.
2. The present writ petition is directed against
the order of black listing of the petitioner firm by order
dated 15.06.2026 passed by respondent no.2.
3. In brief, the facts of the case are that the
petitioner, a proprietorship firm, was awarded a
contract by the respondent-Corporation for
maintenance and supply of 16 skilled and unskilled
persons for an electric sub-station vide contract dated
10.12.2024.
1

UKHC010166192026
2026:UHC:8559-DB
4. The respondent-Corporation initially passed
an order on 27.02.2026 blacklisting the petitioner firm
and debarring it from participating in future contracts
for two years. The said order was subjected to
challenge by the petitioner firm before this Court by
filing WPMB No.244 of 2026. The said writ petition was
allowed by order dated 15.04.2026 on the ground that
the order of blacklisting was passed without notice and
opportunity of hearing to the petitioner.
5. The respondent-Corporation was given liberty
to pass a fresh order after issuing proper notice and
providing opportunity of hearing to the petitioner.
Pursuant thereto, the petitioner was issued a show-cause notice on 24.04.2026. The petitioner replied to
the same on 14.05.2026.
6. The second respondent after considering the
reply has passed the impugned order debarring it from
participating in the future tenders of the Corporation
for a period of two years.
7. The contention of learned counsel for the
petitioner is that there is no finding in the impugned
order that there has been violation of any terms and
conditions of the contract, therefore, the impugned
order is illegal. The further contention is that the
2

UKHC010166192026
2026:UHC:8559-DB
respondents have not held any proper inquiry into the
allegation that ₹1,000/- was realized by the petitioner
firm as commission from the labourers provided by it to
the respondent-Corporation.
8. We have gone through the impugned order
and the material placed on record.
9. The impugned order has been passed on
three grounds, namely:-
1) That one of the labourers, namely, Pramod
Kumar (lineman), out of 16 labourers,
provided by the petitioner, was found
involved in illegal activities and, therefore, he
was removed. Thereafter, the petitioner was
repeatedly asked by notices dated
08.10.2025 and 09.10.2025 to provide his
substitute but the petitioner failed to provide
the same
2) The second ground was that the petitioner
had failed to provide standard quality tools
and kits to the labourers, as per the
agreement, and it compromised the safety of
the labourers.
3) The third ground was that the petitioner
was not paying wages to the labourers in
3

UKHC010166192026
2026:UHC:8559-DB
time and he was charging ₹1,000/- as
commission from them.
10. In respect of the third charge, that the
petitioner was charging ₹1,000/- as commission from
labourers, all 15 labourers had given their affidavits
and which have been taken into consideration while
recording adverse finding against the petitioner.
11. There is no allegation that the labourers, who
had given affidavits against the petitioner, had any
animosity with the petitioner. Therefore, we find no
illegality on part of the respondent Corporation in
relaying on their affidavits.
12. Learned counsel for the petitioner has placed
reliance on a judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court
dated 12.02.2025 passed in Civil Appeal
No.10042/2023 in the case of M/s Techno Prints Vs.
Chhattisgarh Textbook Corporation & Anr.
13. In the said case, the Hon'ble Supreme Court
was examining the validity of a show-cause notice
issued to a contractor requiring him to show-cause as
to why he should not be blacklisted. In the facts of that
case, the Hon'ble Supreme Court was of the opinion
that it was a case of mere breach of contract for which
remedy was provided under the contract and,
4

UKHC010166192026
2026:UHC:8559-DB
therefore, held that the proposed action for blacklisting
was unwarranted.
14. However, in the instant case, as noted above,
there was a serious charge against the petitioner of
realizing commission from the labourers. The
labourers, undoubtedly, belonged to the lower strata of
the society. Under the agreement, there was a specific
stipulation that after deducting EPF, ESI and Insurance
charges from the monthly wages, the remaining
amount would be deposited by the contractor in the
bank accounts of the labourers. The petitioner, in his
explanation, himself stated that he was making
payment partly in cash and partly by deposit in the
bank accounts, which was contrary to the specific
stipulation in the agreement.
15. The contention that inquiry was not got
conducted into the said charge also cannot be
sustained, inasmuch as the affidavits of the labourers
were before the Corporation, relying upon which the
impugned order has been passed.
16. In our opinion, the above charge is sufficient
to sustain the impugned order. Therefore, we are not
examining the other allegations. In any event, the
findings in the impugned order are findings of facts
5

UKHC010166192026
2026:UHC:8559-DB
and, in exercise of writ jurisdiction, we are of the
considered opinion that the said findings do not require
any interference.
17. The writ petition lacks merits and is,
accordingly, dismissed.
18. Pending application, if any, also stands
disposed of.
 (MANOJ KUMAR GUPTA, C. J.)
